Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain in Africa, stands at a height of approximately 19,341 feet (5,895 meters) above sea level.

Mount Kilimanjaro () is a large dormant stratovolcano in Tanzania. It is the highest mountain in Africa and the highest free-standing mountain above sea level in the world, at 5,895 m (19,341 ft) above sea level and 4,900 m (16,100 ft) above its plateau base. Although it is described in classical sources, German missionary Johannes Rebmann is credited as the first European to report the mountain's existence, in 1848. The mountain was incorporated into Kilimanjaro National Park in 1973. This ice cap is rapidly shrinking, with over 80% lost in the 20th century.

How Tall is Mount Kilimanjaro Really? Located on the border between Tanzania and Kenya, Mount Kilimanjaro is situated approximately 340 kilometers (211 miles) southwest of the Tanzanian city of Dar es Salaam.

Mount Everest, for instance, is significantly taller than Kilimanjaro at 8,848 meters.
